complete_brief.subject_context: Every US Submarine Class Ever Built (2026)

facts.claim: USS Holland's interior space was one contiguous compartment.
USS Holland incorporated dual propulsion systems, fixed center of gravity, separate main and auxiliary ballast systems, hydrodynamic shape, and modern weapons system.
USS Holland spent most of her ten years in service at the U.S. Naval Academy as a training submarine.
The Navy purchased USS Holland on April 11, 1900, for $165,000 after two years of trials and modifications.
Admiral Dewey attributed great value to USS Holland's type for harbor and coast defense based on favorable Navy officer reports.
An 1900 agreement gave Vickers a 25-year license to manufacture Holland-class submarines for the UK and Europe using Electric Boat patents.
The U.S. Navy commissioned USS Holland on October 12, 1900, establishing the U.S. Submarine Force.
John P. Holland first demonstrated the Holland VI to the U.S. Navy on 17 March 1898.
The Navy ordered seven more Holland-type boats after trials, which became the A-class submarines with Navy-specified improvements.
USS Holland had one reloadable bow torpedo tube carrying three torpedoes and a pneumatic dynamite gun that was subsequently removed.
